title: Packable credit heuristics — journal
content:
Context / goal:
- Quick personal journal of a 'packable credit' concept: credits that can be bundled into different SKUs (session, burst, retained-cache) and map cleanly back to unit economics.
- Focus: make credits intuitive for devs (mental model) while preserving a tight mapping to GPU/token cost and SLO reservations.

High-level mental model (working):
- Base unit = 250 tokens (micro-credit). Why 250? small enough to be counted across many micro-interactions; packs easily into 1k/5k/10k SKUs.
- Session-credit = 1k tokens + 30s concurrency reservation (useful for chat UIs, guarantees fast cold-starts).
- Burst-credit = 5k tokens, no concurrency guarantee but higher throughput cap.
- Warm-cache-credit = 1k tokens + KV-prefix hit bonus (x0.7 cost) — a separate SKU that signals ops to keep relevant KV cached for customer.

Assumptions (back-of-envelope numbers to sanity-check):
- Baseline model: 13B quant (q4) perf profile: ~500k tokens / GPU-hour (observed in bench).
- Reserve GPU-hour cost assumptions: $2.40 / GPU-hour (aggregated amortized infra + infra margin).
- Therefore cost per 1k tokens = 2.40 / 500 = $0.0048 (~0.48 cents).
- Add infra + orchestration overhead (routing, control plane, observability) ~+20% -> $0.0058 / 1k tokens.
- Margin target for self-serve SKU: 60% gross -> price per 1k tokens ~ $0.0145 (1.45 cents).

Credit <-> money mapping (micro-credit = 250 tokens):
- 250 tokens cost = 0.25 * $0.0058 = $0.00145 (approx $0.0015).
- If we sell micro-credit at 0.005 USD (0.5 cents) -> gross margin is very high (but friction for tiny micropayments).

Pack examples (billable credits and suggested retail):
- Micro pack: 100 micro-credits = 25k tokens -> cost basis = 25 * $0.0058 = $0.145 -> retail $0.40 (margin ~64%).
- Starter dev pack: 5k micro-credits = 1.25M tokens -> cost basis = 1250 * $0.0058 = $7.25 -> retail $18.
- Session-focused: session-credit = 1k tokens + concurrency hint -> map to 4 micro-credits; premium for reservation x1.4. So session-credit retail equivalent = 4 * micro-credit-price * 1.4.
- Burst pack: 5k tokens = 20 micro-credits; bulk discount x0.75.

SLO / capacity signals embedded in credit type (ops implications):
- Session-credit must mark request with 'slot-reserve' attribute. Router will track reserved slots per customer (soft limit).
- Warm-cache-credit signals preload KV-prefix for customer models or pins prefix in LRU for N minutes. Ops surface: we need per-customer cache TTL and accounting.
- If customer uses session-credit but latency breaches SLO, auto-refund logic? (open question)

Edgecases & weirdnesses:
- Users with extremely high-turnover tiny messages (micro-bots) will prefer micro-credit; this increases control-plane overhead. Need amortized accounting to avoid per-call billing overhead. Suggest: throttle per-minute metering; aggregate micro-credits usage per minute per customer into single ledger line.
- Multi-model apps: conversation may mix a cheap embedding + expensive generator -> credit truth must attribute tokens by model class. So credits need an optional dimension: model-tier tag.
- Region multipliers: serving in eu-west may have 1.15x cost factor (data transfer + infra). Credits should carry "region" dimension so redemption applies to correct pool.

Open math checks (to revisit):
- Sensitivity: if throughput is 350k tokens / GPU-hour (worse perf) cost per 1k -> 2.4/350 = $0.00685 -> post overhead $0.0082 -> retail per 1k (60% margin) = $0.0205. So pricing band should be 1.45-2.05 cents / 1k depending on model/quant.
- Cache-hit multiplier assumption (x0.7) is very hand-wavy; need bench to quantify real delta.

SKU names (UX-friendly):
- Credits: micro (250T) | session (1kT + slot) | burst (5kT) | warm (1kT + cache)
- Bundles: Starter, Builder, Team, Scale (scale has seat + reserved throughput).

UX/Docs notes (for devs):
- Simple explanation with punchline: "1 micro-credit ≈ 250 tokens; a typical short chat turn is 1–2 micro-credits."
- Show quick examples in console: "Compose API call estimates: 3 messages * 120 tokens/out = ~360 tokens -> 2 micro-credits (rounded up)"

Billing implications & ledger model (scratch):
- Ledger rows should record: timestamp, customer_id, credit_type, micro_credit_count, model_tier_tag, region_tag. Keep rows compact.
- For session reservation, create a hold row with expiration; convert to debit when consumed or expired (auto-release).
- Aggregation: bill daily for micr-credits consumed; show hourly usage dashboard for debugging.

Questions / TODOs:
- (E) Bench: run warm-cache v cold-cache runs for 3 popular models, capture delta per 1k tokens. -> linear PR linked above.
- (P) UX: language for "session-slot" so customers don't feel like we throttle. Need messaging: "guaranteed instant response" vs "best-effort".
- (O) Ops: TTL for pinned prefixes? 5–15 minutes? tradeoff between cost and UX.
- (Finance) verify margin target vs partner marketplace fees (AWS/GCP marketplace take).

Random scribbles / heuristics I like:
- Price by signal: token cost + concurrency surcharge + cache multiplier + region multiplier + model-tier factor. Keep formula simple in UI: base-credits * multipliers.
- Round credits to 2 decimals only for large packs; for micro usage prefer integer micro-credits.
- Encourage session-credit adoption (simpler mental model for chat apps) by giving a small discount vs per-token micro-credit price.

Notes-to-self:
- Keep names concise. Avoid 'credit' overload—maybe call them 'packets' internally? 'Credits' is fine externally.
- Next iteration: sketch UX flows for 'reserve slot' and 'wallet' in console; include refunds & grace for mid-session model upgrades.

End of entry. Quick attribution: penned while on plane, rough maths, re-check with infra bench before shipping any numbers.
